body:
## See More Without One Giant Filter

A model needs broader context, but one huge filter would add many parameters. Stacking small filters grows the visible region gradually.

The receptive field is the input area that can affect one later value. Pooling or strided convolution reduces spatial size and increases context per value.

Downsampling saves computation but can erase fine detail. Detection and segmentation models often preserve or restore high-resolution paths.
common_mistakes: A CNN requires a separate full model for every pixel.
Stride means the number of class labels.
Padding always deletes the image border.

real_world_usage: CNNs exploit image structure, using fewer parameters than connecting every pixel to every output.
